text:
oncall-bot: Pager triggered — inference-runtime-high-latency for cluster 'hosted-prod-3' (severity: P1). Symptoms: 95th p95 ~ 1.8s, 99th ~ 3.2s; increased KV cache evictions; rollout label: quant-v2-2026-03-16.
Sasha: I'm taking it. pinging Mike and Priya.
Mike: seeing same in grafana. spike starts ~ 1769799000. CPU on workers looks fine, GPU utilization low-ish.
Priya: confirming elevated kv_cache_evictions for model: redwood-3b-quant. eviction rate x10 from baseline.
Zhen: any errors in runtime logs? I'm tailing inference logs now.
Sasha: logs show a lot of "KVCache miss for key: <hex>" repeated and then fallback to full generation path.
Omar: could be compatibility issue introduced with quant-v2 kernel change. Suggest immediate rollback to quant-v1 for hosted-prod-3.
Carla: customer-impact check — APM traces show increased tail latency for 6 external customers; two have >5% error surface increase for requests >2s. Not critical yet, but rising.
Mike: rolling a canary rollback on one shard to quant-v1 now. /deploy rollback --cluster hosted-prod-3 --model redwood-3b-quant --to-tag quant-v1-2026-02-28
(oncall-bot): Deploy rollback job started (job id j-9247). ETA ~ 90s.
Priya: also toggling aggressive prefix caching off for the affected model to reduce miss storm while we validate rollback. Patch: set prefix_cache.enabled=false for redwood-3b-quant on hosted-prod-3.
Sasha: good — add a short TTL on responses metrics so we can observe immediate effect.
Zhen: post-rollback logs show eviction rate dropping within ~30s. p95 trending back toward baseline.
Carla: contacting CS for customer heads-up: message drafted, will send if numbers stay stable for 10m.
Omar: root cause hypothesis: quant-v2 kernel introduced a regression in KV key serialization for long-prefix prompts leading to high effective cache misses and triggering fallback path that is slower. Need repro and unit test.
Mike: rollback completed on primary shard. Job j-9247 succeeded.
(oncall-bot): Pager resolved — incident closed. Duration ~ 0h 25m.
Sasha: post-incident: schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PDT. Action items: 1) Omar to create an isolated repro with the quant-v2 build and a synthetic workload that produces evictions (due EOD). 2) Zhen to add a kvcache serialization unit test + CI gating for quant kernels (due in 3 days). 3) Priya to add a circuit-breaker in runtime that detects missstorm patterns and auto-enable fallback caching tweaks (proposal due in 5 days). 4) Mike to run a performance sweep comparing quant-v1 vs quant-v2 on long-prefix distributions and attach perf artifacts to the postmortem (due in 2 days). 5) Carla to coordinate customer communications and collect impacted customer IDs and request samples (due EOD).
Priya: adding one more — add a dashboard alarm for kv_cache_evictions_rate > 5x baseline sustained for 3m.
Carla: noted, will include in postmortem doc.
Omar: I'll upload the failing trace snippets and the repro script to the incident folder: /incidents/1976543210-quant-evict-repro (will link in the doc).
Sasha: Thanks all. quick follow-up: is there any playbook gap? I noticed our runbook lacked explicit steps for quant rollback; can someone add a short command snippet to the runbook after the postmortem?
Mike: I'll update runbook with rollback command and check the permissions on the deploy service account.
(oncall-bot): Postmortem scheduled: 1769880600 (2026-03-18T16:30:00Z). Meeting link: https://zoom.example/pm-1976543210
Sasha: closing notes — incident resolved, rollback worked, we have action owners and dates. Will run the postmortem and assign follow-ups in the doc. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks everyone, keeping watch for follow-up regressions.
